subject: SLO alignment & deployment sketch for Oscillate AI
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@oscillate.ai>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@oscillate.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO alignment & deployment sketch for Oscillate AI

Thanks for the call today — good conversation. I captured the high-level items below so we have a clear record and next steps. Please call out anything I missed.

Key pain & goals we heard
- Current vendor struggles: unpredictable latency during traffic spikes, opaque unit costs.
- Primary goal: conversational agent at P95 latency <= 150ms (interactive) and P99 <= 500ms for tiered experiences.
- Cost goal: reduce cost-per-session vs current baseline by ~35% while maintaining answer quality.

Traffic & workload signals (from call)
- Sustained: ~120 requests/sec for the recommendation/chat endpoint.
- Burst windows: up to ~600 req/sec for 2-6 minute spikes during peak events.
- Average tokens: ~450 tokens per request (user + assistant + context).
- Mix: ~70% short-answer chat, 20% multi-turn sessions (longer KV cache reuse), 10% embedding/rerank jobs.

Model requirements & quality
- Preference for an open-base model with safety filters; expect to test 2 variants (1 higher-quality, 1 quantized low-cost).
- Need streaming responses for UI; function/tool calls not yet required.

Proposed deployment topology (initial sketch)
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west (pinned capacity) for the chat endpoint to meet P95 targets.
- Autoscale/Burst: Shared hosted capacity fallback to absorb traffic spikes beyond reserved capacity.
- Caching: KV prefix caching for multi-turn sessions + prefix reuse for 70% of tokens to reduce costs.
- Routing: latency-first for interactive endpoints; cost-aware routing for background rerank/embedding jobs.

Operational asks from Oscillate (what we need to size and commit)
- Sample 24-hour request distribution (timestamps + token sizes).
- Current SLA/observability expectations (alerts, SLO burn notifications).
- Security checklist items (SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest/in transit requirements).

Next steps
1) Can you share the sample traffic CSV and SOC2 questionnaire by EOD Tue? (Samir/C. Zhou)
2) Technical deep-dive (1.5h) with Marissa + infra team — proposed Wed 6/23 10:00 PT. Marissa, can you lead sizing and initial capacity model?
3) I'll upload a sketch of the topology and a mutual action plan.

Attachments: oscillate-call-notes.pdf, initial-topology-sketch.png, MAP_Oscillate.xlsx

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0168

From: Samir Patel <samir@oscillate.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@oscillate.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO alignment & deployment sketch for Oscillate AI

Diego — thanks for the clear notes, looks right. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Traffic: the sustained ~120 r/s number is our production baseline for the US region only; EU is smaller (10-15 r/s) for now. Peaks are CDN-triggered (marketing blasts) and can hit ~600 r/s for ~3-5 minutes.
- Token distribution: mean ~450, median ~320, 95th ~900 (long-form generation seen in support flows).
- Latency: P95 150ms is our front-line target; for interactive chat we need P99 < 500ms when possible (not strict for background rerank).
- Security: we need a completed SOC2 questionnaire and evidence of encryption at rest. Can you provide your standard questionnaire and a timeline for SOC artifacts?

We attached a 24h sample export (I’ll send the CSV via the secure link) and added a short note about our peak patterns.

Happy to take the proposed 6/23 slot — confirm with calendar invite. Also, on cost: we are sensitive to burst bills, so please include any recommended burst-limits or cost-smoothing options in the runbook.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Oscillate AI
samir@oscillate.ai | +1 628-555-0100

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@oscillate.ai>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@oscillate.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLO alignment & deployment sketch for Oscillate AI

Marissa/Rachel — looping you in for the technical deep-dive. Samir confirmed traffic and SOC ask. Please prep: 
- Capacity model (workload -> GPU count mapping) with assumptions for quantized vs FP16 variants.
- Proposed Dedicated pool sizing and autoscale policy that keeps P95 <150ms at baseline and options for handling 600 r/s spikes (burst vs fallback).
- Short security artifact list we can provide quickly (SOC2 report summary + encryption statements).

I’ve attached the topology sketch and MAP. We have a tentative 6/23 10:00 PT deep-dive — Marissa, can you take the calendar lead and I’ll invite the Oscillate infra folks?

On quoting Samir: 
> "Peaks are CDN-triggered (marketing blasts) and can hit ~600 r/s for ~3-5 minutes."

Thanks — Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@oscillate.ai>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@oscillate.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO alignment & deployment sketch for Oscillate AI

Got it — I’ll lead the deep-dive on 6/23 10:00 PT. Initial notes: 
- I attached capacity-model-v1.xlsx with a baseline estimate: ~4 x A100-equivalent GPUs to meet the 120 r/s P95 target at FP16 with conservative KV cache reuse. With 8-bit quantized runtime we can reduce to ~3 GPUs but will need to validate quality tradeoffs.
- For handling 600 r/s spikes: recommend 2-tier approach — (1) short-term burst into hosted shared capacity with cost caps, (2) optional pre-warming of reserved capacity before scheduled marketing events (MAP automation).
- Security: we can provide SOC2 Type II summary and an encryption statement within 48 hours; full artifacts available under NDA. I’ll attach the standard questionnaire (security-questionnaire-oscillate.pdf) and the capacity workbook.

Asks before the deep-dive: 
1) Sample 24h CSV with token sizes and timestamp buckets (Samir)
2) A few example request payloads so we can validate tokenization and prompt-size behavior
3) Clarify whether streaming is required for all endpoints or only interactive chat UI (this affects latency model)

I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda by EOD Monday.

—Marissa
